São Vicente — Lisbon, Portugal

Relatively safer day Average night

In detail

Covers Graça and the Santa Apolónia area. No serious violent-crime coverage names São Vicente specifically; the parish council itself told a 2025 Observador special report that it believes the 'feeling of insecurity has increased more than actual criminality', citing only pickpocketing on trams and occasional distraction thefts at outdoor cafés. One dated incident stands out — 47 parked cars were vandalised in Graça in November 2024 — but this reads as an isolated dispute rather than a recurring pattern. The overall documented concern is limited and non-violent, so day is rated green and night a light yellow. Sources checked: Público, 17 Nov 2024 – "Danificadas 47 viaturas na Graça, em Lisboa"; Observador (special report) – "Droga, violência e uma bala perdida. Juntas de Lisboa pedem mais segurança na cidade" (São Vicente parish council quote on perception vs. crime, tram pickpocketing).

Frequently asked questions

Is São Vicente safe?

Wandroz currently rates São Vicente in Lisbon, Portugal as relatively safer than most other areas covered on Wandroz during the day and roughly average compared to other areas covered on Wandroz at night. This is a qualitative first-pass assessment based on general local knowledge and public reputation, not an official geolocated crime dataset — see the note on data limitations below before treating it as more precise than it is.

Is São Vicente safe at night?

At night, São Vicente is rated as roughly average compared to other areas covered on Wandroz. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is São Vicente a good area to stay in as a tourist?

São Vicente's day rating (relatively safer than most other areas covered on Wandroz) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
